name: Paper Admiral
lore: Folded from yesterday's news. Commands a fleet of one.
rationale: Reads at 16x16 as a folded newspaper hat: a flat top crease, two short bars of newsprint, a widening white crown, and a solid dark cuff along the bottom edge. The cuff is the whole trick — it is the one shape that says 'folded paper' instead of 'cloth cap', which is what keeps it clear of Sprout Cap and Straw Sunhat. Three values only (paper, fold shadow, ink), so it stays legible against any DNA body color. Slot semantics relied on: hats composite LAST and paint OVER the Pal, so the piece can be fully opaque and never has to dodge the body. I authored it in rows 1-4 only, and both empty rows are deliberate — row 0 stays clear so the wisp adult's (0,-1) hat shift does not slice off the top crease, and row 5 stays clear so the brim never reaches the eye rows on blob/quad/jelly/avian adults. Simulated against all 27 archetype x stage combos using the real CosmeticOffset table: 40/40 cells land on eight archetypes, 35/40 on shell, whose (-4,+5) offset clips every shipped hat the same way. No shiny accent, matching the shipped pattern where '*' rides the coin rares and the relics. 40 painted cells.

name: Moth Hour
lore: They think you're the porch light. Every night, all three of them, absolutely certain.
rationale: Reads as three moths orbiting the Pal's head, with pale specks drifting down past its flanks. Each moth is a four-cell glyph — a three-wide wing pair (pale, dark body, pale) with a shadowed lower wing tucked under the center — and that structure is what separates this from all six shipped auras, which are single-pixel dither. It is the first aura with a recognizable shape in it. Slot semantics relied on, and the hard part: auras composite BEHIND the body and are occluded wherever the Pal is painted, so guessing placement would have quietly buried the moths. I mapped every cell that is transparent on all 27 archetype x stage silhouettes after the aura's stage shift (0,+2 baby / 0,+1 teen / 0,0 adult), then placed all three glyphs only in pockets free in every single one. Result: no moth ever loses a cell on any body at any stage; worst case is 21/25 cells and the four missing ones are baby-shift clipping at the bottom margin, never a broken moth. The single '*' is a moth's body at row 3 col 14, a cell verified never occluded on any of the 27, so the shiny sparkle always lands. Sparse by construction — 25 painted cells, never more than four in a row, so it rings the creature instead of becoming the blob the composition order warns about.

name: Wander Bell
lore: Some weeks the stall has one; most weeks the hook is bare. It goes where it likes and comes back when it likes, which the keepers agree is exactly what a bell called Wander ought to do.
rationale: Owner decision 2026-07-25: priced as a rare (900) rather than the elder-1 trophy, because scarf-thirty-winters took that milestone in game v1.8.1. The name now describes real behaviour: the piece is only in stock on some weeks (see the wandering-stock mechanic and its BarnCheck block), never lost forever. Art unchanged and still verified: reads as a worn leather cord with a small brass bell over the chest, thin collar rather than a woven band so it does not crowd the six shipped scarves, cord on rows 8-9 to match the per-archetype neck anchors, bell hanging 10-13 clear of every archetype's eye rows; 44/44 cells land on eight archetypes and 42/44 on shell, and it stacks cleanly under Paper Admiral since hats composite after scarves.
